name: Magnetic Gaze+Pinch
summary: Gaze+Pinch where each target has a larger invisible field; a pinch while gaze is inside the field snaps the selection to the target, so a pinch that comes slightly before gaze arrives still selects it.
howItWorks: The spatial field (20 distance-independent millimetres) targets early-trigger errors. In the study with 9 expert users it rescued by far the most would-be errors, but users adapted by pinching less precisely and earlier, relying on the snap; throughput, time and final error rate did not differ from plain Gaze+Pinch.
advantages: Corrects early pinches; users could select less precisely.
limitations: Users came to rely on it, which may cause wrong picks in dense layouts.

relationships.note: Adds a snapping field around each target.
Sticky and Magnetic were introduced and compared in the same study.
